claims.citation: New York Herald, 24 May 1866, p. 5, col. 5
claims.verbatim:
Ship Caravan, Marshall, Liverpool, 65[?] days, with mdse and
65[?] passengers, to Howland & Frothingham. Encountered
very heavy W and NW gales to lon 61. March 29 during a
hard gale from N, was struck by a sea on the starboard
quarter, which swept the mate from the poop to the main
deck, severely bruising him about the arms and legs; carried
away rails from poop, filling all the rooms in the cabin and
breaking most of the windows; April 30, during a hurricane,
in a head sea, ship sprung a leak at the rate of 1000[?] strokes
per hour, which kept the crew constantly pumping to the 5th[?]
inst, when they became exhausted; was obliged to hire 12[?]
of the passengers to keep on pumping; same day, discovered
the rudder post sprung; 10th[?] inst, during a heavy gale, car-
ried away all the steering gear; was obliged to steer[?] ship with
the canvass until the rudder was secured; since, then have
steered by means of tackles, and it has been with the great-
est difficulty the ship was brought into port.
